items.title: Ministers Alty, Gull-Masty, Chartrand, and Valdez issue a statement on Sisters in Spirit Day and the National Day of Action for Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women, Girls and 2SLGBTQI+ people
items.content_text: On Sisters in Spirit Day, we honour and remember all the Indigenous women, girls and 2SLGBTQI+ people who have gone missing or been murdered. We stand with the survivors, families, and communities whose advocacy, leadership and determination continue to drive action and accountability, and we recommit ourselves to ending this violence.

items.title: Joint Statement on the Anniversary of the Snapback of UN Restrictions on and related to Iran
items.content_text: “On September 27, 2025 (at 8:00 p.m. EDT), six United Nations Security Council resolutions (UNSCRs) – 1696 (2006), 1737 (2006), 1747 (2007), 1803 (2008), 1835 (2008), 1929 (2010) – returned into force pursuant to the completion of the snapback process. France, Germany, and the United Kingdom initiated this process in response to Tehran’s persistent and significant non-performance of its nuclear commitments under the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA).

items.content_text: The unlawful deportation and forcible transfer of Ukrainian children, the unlawful detention of civilians, and the treatment of prisoners of war are among the gravest consequences of Russia’s unprovoked and unjustifiable full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

items.title: Tribunal Initiates Expiry Review—Certain Small Power Transformers from Chinese Taipei and Korea
items.content_text: The Canadian International Trade Tribunal today initiated an expiry review (RR-2026-007) of its finding made on December 24, 2021, in inquiry NQ-2021-003, to determine if the expiry of the finding is likely to lead to continued or resumed dumping of certain small power transformers from Chinese Taipei and Korea and is likely to result in injury to the domestic industry.

items.title: National Film Board of Canada featured in the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art’s inaugural film program. Landmark films by Norman McLaren, Arthur Lipsett, Jean-Claude Labrecque and Theodore Ushev are among 19 NFB titles selected for stunning new museum experience in Los Angeles.
items.content_text: The National Film Board of Canada (NFB) has been chosen to be part of the inaugural film program at the new Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles, where 19 NFB works will be featured in continuous screenings in the museum’s two theatres. Founded by George Lucas and Mellody Hobson, the museum opened its doors on September 22.

items.title: Minister Dabrusin advances Canada–China cooperation on climate, clean growth, and the environment
items.content_text: For more than 30 years, Canada and China have worked together on the environment. This week, Canada’s Minister of the Environment, Climate Change and Nature, the Honourable Julie Dabrusin, led Canada’s delegation to the Annual General Meeting of the China Council for International Cooperation on Environment and Development (CCICED), which took place in Beijing, China, from September 27 to 29, 2026.

items.title: Public hearing on Pickering Nuclear Generating Station and Waste Management Facility
items.content_text: Ottawa, Ontario – Part 2 of a 2-part public hearing held by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC) will take place from October 6 to 9, 2026, to consider an application from Ontario Power Generation (OPG) to renew the power reactor operating licence for the Pickering Nuclear Generating Station (PNGS) and the waste facility operating licence for the Pickering Waste Management Facility. The Commission will also consider the proposed refurbishment of PNGS Units 5 to 8.
